--- title: "Hardly any graduates studied a major less AI-exposed than the average occupation" subtitle: "2,431,833 graduates with measured earnings across 285 bachelor's majors. Each step adds the share of graduates from majors with that exposure score." description: "Only 3.5% of 2.43 million measured graduates studied a major less AI-exposed than the average occupation on the AIOE index. A graduate-weighted cumulative step curve replaces the original chart's percentile axis with the index's raw scale. Built in R with ggplot2, ggtext, showtext and ggview." date: "2026-10-19" author: - name: "Steven Ponce" url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app" citation: url: "https://stevenponce.netlify.app/data_visualizations/TidyTuesday/2026/tt_2026_42.html" categories: ["TidyTuesday", "2026"] tags: [ "College Majors", "AI Exposure", "AIOE", "College Scorecard", "Higher Education", "Labor Market", "Cumulative Distribution", "Step Chart", "Weighted ECDF", "Annotation", "ggtext", "showtext", "ggview", "2026" ] image: "thumbnails/tt_2026_42.png" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 5 code-link: true code-fold: true code-tools: true code-summary: "Show code" editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline execute: freeze: true cache: true error: false message: false warning: false eval: true --- ![Cumulative step chart titled "Hardly any graduates studied a major less AI-exposed than the average occupation." At the index's zero line, the curve reaches only 3.5%: 3.5% of 2,431,833 graduates with measured earnings studied one of the 31 bachelor's majors scoring below the average occupation on the AI Occupational Exposure (AIOE) index, highlighted in burgundy. The horizontal axis shows the AIOE score from about −1.3 to +1.5, with zero marking the unweighted average across 774 occupations. The vertical axis shows the cumulative share of measured graduates across 285 majors. To the right of zero, the curve climbs: a single step at +0.44, Registered Nursing, adds 17.6% of graduates, and the curve crosses 50% at about +1.07. Exposure measures overlap with AI abilities, not job displacement. Data: College Scorecard, AIOE (Felten, Raj and Seamans 2021), NCES/BLS CIP-SOC crosswalk.](tt_2026_42.png){#fig-1} ### [**Steps to Create this Graphic**]{.mark} #### [1. Load Packages & Setup]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: load #| warning: false #| message: false #| results: "hide" ## 1. LOAD PACKAGES & SETUP ---- suppressPackageStartupMessages({ if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman") pacman::p_load( tidyverse, ggtext, showtext, janitor, scales, glue, ggview, magick ) }) # Source utility functions suppressMessages(source(here::here("R/utils/fonts.R"))) source(here::here("R/utils/social_icons.R")) source(here::here("R/utils/image_utils.R")) source(here::here("R/themes/base_theme.R")) ``` ```` ::: #### [2. Read in the Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: read #| include: true #| eval: true #| warning: false ### |- figure settings ---- fig_w <- 10 fig_h <- 6.5 fig_dpi <- 320 out_file <- "2026/Week_42/2026_42.png" setup_fonts() fonts <- get_font_families() title_family <- fonts$title_1 %||% fonts$title text_family <- fonts$text ## 2. READ IN THE DATA ---- tt <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load(2026, week = 42) majors_raw <- tt$ai_salary_majors |> clean_names() rm(tt) ``` ```` ::: #### [3. Examine the Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: examine #| include: true #| eval: true #| results: 'hide' #| warning: false ## 3. EXAMINING THE DATA ---- glimpse(majors_raw) skimr::skim(majors_raw) ``` ```` ::: #### [4. Tidy Data]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: tidy #| warning: false ### |- majors ---- majors <- majors_raw |> mutate(is_rn = str_detect(field_of_study, "^Registered Nursing")) ### |- weighted ECDF: aggregate tied scores, then one step per distinct score ---- ecdf_df <- majors |> summarise( grads = sum(n_graduates), n_maj = n(), has_rn = any(is_rn), .by = ai_exposure ) |> arrange(ai_exposure) |> mutate( cum_share = cumsum(grads) / sum(grads), prev_share = lag(cum_share, default = 0) ) x_min <- -1.3 x_max <- 1.5 step_df <- bind_rows( tibble(ai_exposure = x_min, cum_share = 0), ecdf_df |> select(ai_exposure, cum_share), tibble(ai_exposure = x_max, cum_share = 1) ) |> mutate(side = if_else(ai_exposure < 0, "below", "above")) # Split the step path at zero so the left segment can carry the accent share_at_zero <- max(ecdf_df$cum_share[ecdf_df$ai_exposure < 0]) step_below <- bind_rows( step_df |> filter(ai_exposure < 0), tibble(ai_exposure = 0, cum_share = share_at_zero) ) step_above <- bind_rows( tibble(ai_exposure = 0, cum_share = share_at_zero), step_df |> filter(ai_exposure >= 0) ) ### |- reader-facing numbers (computed, guarded next to the copy they feed) ---- total_grads <- sum(majors$n_graduates) n_majors <- nrow(majors) n_below_zero <- sum(majors$ai_exposure < 0) share_below <- sum(majors$n_graduates[majors$ai_exposure < 0]) / total_grads rn_row <- ecdf_df |> filter(has_rn) rn_exp <- rn_row$ai_exposure rn_share <- majors$n_graduates[majors$is_rn] / total_grads # Graduate-weighted median: first exposure score where cumulative share >= 50% half_row <- ecdf_df |> filter(cum_share >= 0.5) |> slice_head(n = 1) x_half <- half_row$ai_exposure med_major <- median(majors$ai_exposure) # equal-weight median ``` ```` ::: #### [5. Visualization Parameters]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: params #| include: true #| warning: false ### |- plot aesthetics ---- colors <- get_theme_colors( palette = list( accent = "#722F37", curve = "#5c5f5b", ink = "#22282b", muted = "#7A7068", paper = "#f4f1ea" ) ) clrs <- colors$palette if (is.null(clrs$accent)) { clrs <- list( accent = "#722F37", curve = "#5c5f5b", ink = "#22282b", muted = "#7A7068", paper = "#f4f1ea" ) } col_accent <- clrs$accent col_curve <- clrs$curve col_ink <- clrs$ink col_muted <- clrs$muted col_paper <- clrs$paper ### |- titles and caption ---- title_text <- "Hardly any graduates studied a major less AI-exposed than the average occupation" subtitle_text <- str_glue( "{comma(total_grads)} graduates with measured earnings across {n_majors} bachelor's majors.\n", "Each step adds the share of graduates from majors with that exposure score." ) # Provenance constant (not computed from this dataset): AIOE Data Appendix A n_aioe_occupations <- 774 note_text <- paste( "Exposure is the unweighted mean of linked occupational AIOE scores.", glue("Index zero is the unweighted average across {n_aioe_occupations} occupations."), "The supplied CIP-SOC crosswalk mixes SOC 2018 mappings with SOC 2010 exposure codes,", "potentially omitting occupations whose codes changed.", "Exposure measures task overlap, not job displacement.", "Graduates = those with measured earnings one year after graduation.
" ) caption_text <- create_social_caption( tt_year = 2026, tt_week = 42, source_text = "College Scorecard (US Dept. of Education) · AIOE (Felten, Raj & Seamans 2021) · NCES/BLS CIP-SOC crosswalk" ) caption_full <- paste0(note_text, "
", caption_text) ### |- annotation text (built from guarded values) ---- lab_below_big <- percent(share_below, accuracy = 0.1) lab_below_small <- glue("of measured graduates studied one of the\n{n_below_zero} majors scoring below the index's zero reference") lab_rn <- glue("Registered Nursing alone:\n{percent(rn_share, accuracy = 0.1)} of measured graduates") lab_half <- "Half of measured\ngraduates" lab_zero <- "Index average (zero)" ### |- copy guards ---- all_copy <- c(title_text, subtitle_text, note_text, lab_below_small, lab_rn, lab_half, lab_zero) ### |- plot theme ---- base_theme <- create_base_theme(colors) weekly_theme <- extend_weekly_theme( base_theme, theme( plot.background = element_rect(fill = col_paper, color = NA), panel.background = element_rect(fill = col_paper, color = NA), plot.title = element_text( family = title_family, face = "bold", size = rel(1.42), color = col_ink, lineheight = 1.05, margin = margin(b = 8) ), plot.subtitle = element_text( family = text_family, size = rel(0.92), color = col_muted, lineheight = 1.2, margin = margin(b = 16) ), plot.caption = element_textbox_simple( family = text_family, size = rel(0.62), color = col_muted, lineheight = 1.3, width = unit(1, "npc"), margin = margin(t = 14) ), plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption.position = "plot", axis.title.x = element_text( family = text_family, color = col_muted, size = rel(0.85), margin = margin(t = 10) ), axis.title.y = element_text( family = text_family, color = col_muted, size = rel(0.85), margin = margin(r = 10) ), axis.text = element_text(family = text_family, color = col_muted, size = rel(0.8)), axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#ddd5c6", linewidth = 0.3), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(20, 28, 14, 20) ) ) theme_set(weekly_theme) ``` ```` ::: #### [6. Plot]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: plot #| warning: false ### |- annotation positions ---- pos <- list( below_x = -1.22, below_big_y = 0.30, below_small_y = 0.215, below_pt_x = 0, below_pt_y = share_below, rn_x = rn_exp + 0.04, rn_y = (rn_row$prev_share + rn_row$cum_share) / 2, # right of its riser, below the plateau half_x = x_half, half_lab_x = x_half - 0.22, half_lab_y = 0.62, zero_lab_y = 0.98 ) ### |- main plot ---- p <- ggplot() + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = col_ink, linewidth = 0.6) + geom_step( data = step_above, aes(ai_exposure, cum_share), direction = "hv", color = col_curve, linewidth = 0.75 ) + geom_step( data = step_below, aes(ai_exposure, cum_share), direction = "hv", color = col_accent, linewidth = 1.3 ) + annotate("point", x = pos$below_pt_x, y = pos$below_pt_y, color = col_accent, size = 3 ) + annotate("text", x = pos$below_x, y = pos$below_big_y, label = lab_below_big, family = title_family, fontface = "bold", size = 11, color = col_accent, hjust = 0, vjust = 0 ) + annotate("text", x = pos$below_x, y = pos$below_small_y, label = lab_below_small, family = text_family, size = 3.6, color = col_ink, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, lineheight = 1.15 ) + annotate("text", x = 0.03, y = pos$zero_lab_y, label = lab_zero, family = text_family, size = 3.1, color = col_ink, hjust = 0 ) + annotate("text", x = pos$rn_x, y = pos$rn_y, label = lab_rn, family = text_family, size = 3.1, color = col_muted, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.15 ) + annotate("point", x = pos$half_x, y = 0.5, color = col_ink, size = 2) + annotate("segment", x = pos$half_lab_x + 0.02, xend = pos$half_x - 0.02, y = pos$half_lab_y - 0.03, yend = 0.51, color = col_muted, linewidth = 0.3 ) + annotate("text", x = pos$half_lab_x, y = pos$half_lab_y, label = lab_half, family = text_family, size = 3.1, color = col_muted, hjust = 1, vjust = 0, lineheight = 1.1 ) + scale_x_continuous( limits = c(x_min, x_max), breaks = seq(-1, 1.5, 0.5), labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.02)) ) + scale_y_continuous( limits = c(0, 1), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03)) ) + labs( title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, caption = caption_full, x = "AI exposure of the occupations linked to a major (AIOE score) more exposed \u2192", y = "Cumulative share of measured graduates" ) ``` ```` ::: ### [7. Save]{.smallcaps} ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: save #| warning: false ### |- save ---- main_path <- here::here("data_visualizations", "TidyTuesday", "2026", "tt_2026_42.png") thumb_path <- here::here("data_visualizations", "TidyTuesday", "2026", "thumbnails", "tt_2026_42.png") # Full-size version, for the QMD figure ggview::save_ggplot(plot = p, file = main_path, width = fig_w, height = fig_h, units = "in", dpi = fig_dpi) # Reduced-size thumbnail, for the YAML `image:` field fs::dir_create(dirname(thumb_path)) magick::image_read(main_path) |> magick::image_resize("400") |> magick::image_write(thumb_path) ``` ```` ::: #### [8.
